title: Make columns with grid-template-columns
why_it_matters: It is the first step to any grid layout.
explanation: Setting display: grid and grid-template-columns creates columns. Each value is one column width. The fr unit means a fraction of the free space, so 1fr 1fr 1fr makes three equal columns that fill the row.
try_it: Put six boxes inside a grid container and turn them into three equal columns.

title: Before vs after: repeat() for columns
why_it_matters: Long column lists become short and easy to change.
explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) means the same as 1fr 1fr 1fr. The first number is how many times to repeat and the second is the track size. It keeps long column lists short and easy to edit.
try_it: Change a grid from 4 columns to 6 by editing only the number inside repeat().

title: Quiz: how wide is 2fr next to 1fr?
why_it_matters: It shows how fr units share space.
explanation: Question: in grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr, how wide is the second column? Answer: twice as wide as the first. The fr unit splits the leftover space in proportion, so 1fr 2fr gives one third and two thirds.
try_it: Try 1fr 3fr and 2fr 1fr and watch how the column widths change.

title: Common mistake: 1fr columns that overflow
why_it_matters: It fixes grids that stretch past their container.
explanation: A plain 1fr column cannot shrink below its content, so a wide image or long word can stretch the grid. Writing minmax(0, 1fr) lets the column shrink to fit and keeps the layout inside its container.
try_it: Put a very long unbroken word in a 1fr column, then fix the overflow with minmax(0, 1fr).

title: grid-auto-rows sets the height of new rows
why_it_matters: Every row in a gallery can match without extra code.
explanation: Grid creates rows automatically as items need them. Use grid-auto-rows to set the height of those automatic rows. A fixed height or a minmax() range keeps every row in a card gallery consistent.
try_it: Add nine items to a three-column grid and give every row the same height.

title: Name your layout with grid-template-areas
why_it_matters: The CSS reads like a picture of the page.
explanation: grid-template-areas lets you draw the layout with words. Each quoted string is a row, and each word is a cell. Give items a matching grid-area name and they land in the right place.
try_it: Draw a header, sidebar and main area with grid-template-areas on a blank page.

title: span lets an item cover several columns
why_it_matters: Featured cards can be wider without extra markup.
explanation: grid-column: span 2 tells an item to cover two columns, starting wherever it naturally lands. The grid moves the other items around it. It is an easy way to make one card stand out.
try_it: Make the first card in a three-column grid span two columns.

title: grid-column: 1 / -1 spans the full row
why_it_matters: Banners stretch across any number of columns.
explanation: Grid lines are numbered from 1 at the left edge. A value of -1 means the last line. So grid-column: 1 / -1 stretches an item across every explicit column, however many there are.
try_it: Add a banner to a grid and make it span all columns with 1 / -1.

title: auto-fit vs auto-fill
why_it_matters: It decides what happens to leftover space.
explanation: Both keywords create as many columns as fit. With few items, auto-fill keeps empty columns and leaves blank space. auto-fit collapses the empty columns, so the real items stretch to fill the row.
try_it: Show only two cards in this grid and compare auto-fit with auto-fill.

title: minmax() sets a minimum and a maximum
why_it_matters: Tracks can flex without getting too small or too big.
explanation: minmax(150px, 300px) makes a track at least 150px and at most 300px, depending on the space available. Pair it with 1fr as the maximum to let a track grow while keeping a sensible minimum.
try_it: Resize the window and watch the first column stay between 150px and 300px.

title: Common mistake: minmax() overflow on phones
why_it_matters: A 250px minimum breaks screens narrower than 250px.
explanation: If the container is narrower than the minimum in minmax(250px, 1fr), the column overflows. Wrapping the minimum in min(250px, 100%) caps it at the container width, so the grid never overflows.
try_it: Test your card grid at 200px wide in DevTools and apply the min() fix if it overflows.

title: Subgrid lines up content inside cards
why_it_matters: Titles and buttons align even when text lengths differ.
explanation: grid-template-rows: subgrid lets a nested grid reuse its parent's rows. Cards that each hold a title, text and button can then line up across a row. It works in all current major browsers.
try_it: Make three cards with different text lengths and align their buttons using subgrid.

title: justify-items and align-items in a grid
why_it_matters: You can place content inside each cell.
explanation: In a grid, justify-items aligns each item horizontally inside its cell and align-items does it vertically. The default is stretch. Set both to center and every item sits in the middle of its cell.
try_it: Set justify-items to start, center, then end and watch the items move in their cells.

title: place-content centers the whole grid
why_it_matters: It positions the tracks when they are smaller than the box.
explanation: If your columns total less than the container, the extra space sits at the end. justify-content and align-content move the whole grid. place-content: center is the shorthand for both.
try_it: Make a small grid inside a tall box and center it with place-content.

title: grid-auto-flow: dense fills the holes
why_it_matters: Mixed-size tiles pack without gaps.
explanation: When some items span several columns, empty spaces can appear. grid-auto-flow: dense lets later items fill those holes. Be careful, because it changes the visual order away from the HTML order.
try_it: Add a few wide tiles to a grid and toggle dense on and off to see the holes.

title: aspect-ratio keeps a box in shape
why_it_matters: It ends the old padding-top percentage hack.
explanation: aspect-ratio sets the proportion between width and height. With width: 100% and aspect-ratio: 16 / 9, the box keeps its shape as the screen changes. It is ideal for videos and thumbnails.
try_it: Make a 16 / 9 placeholder box and shrink the window to see it keep its shape.

title: Common mistake: aspect-ratio plus a height
why_it_matters: It explains why the ratio seems ignored.
explanation: aspect-ratio only works when one side is automatic. If you set both width and height, the ratio is ignored because both sizes are already fixed. Remove the height and let the ratio calculate it.
try_it: Set a width and aspect-ratio on a box, then delete its height.

title: Myth: grid replaces flexbox
why_it_matters: It helps you use both for what they do best.
explanation: Myth: once you learn grid, flexbox is obsolete. Grid lays out rows and columns together, while flexbox arranges items along one line. Real pages mix them, grid for the page and flexbox inside components.
try_it: Find one grid and one flex layout in a site you like using DevTools.

title: Grid starts from the layout, flex from content
why_it_matters: It gives you a quick rule for picking one.
explanation: With grid you usually define the tracks first and place content into them. With flexbox the content decides how much space it takes. If you need things to line up in both directions, reach for grid.
try_it: Sketch a layout and decide for each part whether it is a line of items or a grid.

title: Before vs after: holy grail layout with grid
why_it_matters: Header, sidebar, content and footer need no hacks.
explanation: Grid can build a header, sidebar, main area and footer with a few lines. The middle row takes the leftover height with 1fr, which keeps the footer at the bottom on short pages.
try_it: Build this page layout, then check that the footer stays at the bottom on short content.

title: justify-self moves one grid item
why_it_matters: You can break a single item out of the group alignment.
explanation: justify-items sets the default for every item, and justify-self overrides it for one. Use align-self for the vertical direction. It is helpful for badges or buttons that need a different position.
try_it: Align every item to the start, then push one button to the end with justify-self.

title: Project idea: a photo gallery with big tiles
why_it_matters: It practices spans and dense packing in one build.
explanation: Build a photo gallery in a four-column grid where a few photos span two columns or two rows. Use gap for spacing and grid-auto-flow: dense so the tiles pack without holes. Then check it on a phone.
try_it: Pick twelve images and decide which three should be the big tiles.

title: Project idea: a dashboard with named areas
why_it_matters: It practices grid-template-areas and responsive changes.
explanation: Design a dashboard with a header, sidebar, stats row and a chart area using grid-template-areas. Then change the area names inside a media query so the sidebar moves below the content on narrow screens.
try_it: Write the area map on paper for desktop and for mobile before you code it.

title: Quiz: where do extra grid items go?
why_it_matters: It explains explicit versus implicit tracks.
explanation: Question: a grid has two columns and five items, but no rows are defined. How many rows appear? Answer: three. Rows you did not define are called implicit, and grid-auto-rows sizes them.
try_it: Add a sixth and a seventh item and count the implicit rows in DevTools.

title: Debug grids with the DevTools overlay
why_it_matters: You see the lines, gaps and area names directly.
explanation: In Chrome and Firefox DevTools, elements with display: grid show a grid badge in the Elements panel. Click it to draw an overlay with line numbers and area names, which makes placement mistakes easy to see.
try_it: Turn on the grid overlay for any grid and enable line numbers.
